description: List daylight saving time (DST) clock changes for one city. Use when the user asks when the clocks change, or whether a recurring meeting moves when DST starts or ends. Defaults to the next year. Each change includes the local time and the ISO week and US week of that local date. The range can be at most 366 days.

city.description: One city: a name, a city id from a city search, an IANA time zone such as Europe/Copenhagen, or a zone abbreviation or fixed offset such as EST, CET, UTC or UTC+2. A comma adds a region, state or country to that one city, for example "Paris, France", "Paris, TX" or "Munich, Bavaria"; it is not a second city. Multiple cities must be separate list items, for example ["Berlin","Rome"]. Spelling and accents are flexible. When several cities share a name, the best match from the site search is used and the others come back in alternatives.

end_date.description: Last day, YYYY-MM-DD. Defaults to 365 days later. Also accepted: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM, YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ, YYYY/MM/DD, or YYYYMMDD.

start_date.description: First day, YYYY-MM-DD. Defaults to today (UTC). Also accepted: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM, YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ, YYYY/MM/DD, or YYYYMMDD.

name: get_dst_changes

alternatives.description: Other cities that matched the same name, after the best-ranked city was chosen. The order is the site search order: match, then priority, then population.

weeks.description: ISO week (Monday start; week 1 contains the year's first Thursday) and US week (Sunday start; 1 January is week 1 of that calendar year).

zone_notes.description: Present when a city argument was a time zone abbreviation or fixed offset such as EST or UTC+2. Says which time zone it was read as, and what else the abbreviation can mean.

title: Daylight-saving changes
